content.heading: No need to leave what you’re doing.
body: And when you’re working somewhere else…
That sentence doesn’t sound quite like you. Highlight it and ask Merlin for another version. Put it back when it feels right.
Or ask about a webpage, a file in Finder, or what’s on your screen, with your permission.

Scripted example: open Merlin in Photoshop and ask how to remove a background. Approve the sample screen request. Merlin sees the screenshot and explains which tool to use. The demo user clicks Remove Background and Photoshop adds a mask. This demo never captures your screen or changes your files.

items.title: What can Merlin help me with?
items.body: Merlin is an AI chief of staff for your Mac. It helps with browser research and tasks, meetings, files, coding projects, connected services, and scheduled or event-driven routines. Companion brings that help into the apps you’re already using.

items.title: What do I need to get started?
items.body: Sign in, connect your email and calendar, tell Merlin about your priorities, and start your trial. The desktop setup then walks you through the permissions needed for Companion. Email and calendar connections are required in the current onboarding experience.

items.title: Can I use Merlin in my own browser?
items.body: Yes. Pair the browser extension to use your existing browser sessions, or work in Merlin’s built-in browser. You can follow a task, stop it, or take over.

items.title: How does Companion work?
items.body: Press Option + Space to open Companion over your current app. Ask about your work, use selected text as context, or approve a screen capture when Merlin needs to see what’s on screen.

items.title: Can Merlin help with meeting notes?
items.body: The Meetings tab brings recordings, speaker-labelled transcripts, and notes together. You can search meetings, organize them in folders, and use templates to refine your notes.
